Regular, a Medium, a SemiBold and a Bold, each with an italic - and
every one of them carries 'Cormorant Garamond' as name ID 1. The one
file in fonts/ is the Regular. Asking for the bare family name would
therefore be asking for whichever cut a machine happens to have, and
the local() route below is precisely where that would happen, so the
full name (name ID 4) is what gets declared instead - the same answer
texturina-18pt-regular and the two Telegraf packs reached, for their
It is worth more here than the single shipped file suggests. Cormorant

_comment_metrics: One number about this face reaches the channel that uses it, and it
is written down here because it is the face's and not the channel's.
The x-height is 386 units of a 1000-unit em, against a cap height of
625. That is a Garamond: the lower case is small relative to the
capitals and the ascenders run well past them, which is what the
letterforms are for and not a defect to be corrected with a larger
size. At the Snapchat preset's stated 40px it comes out as a 15.4px
x-height where Telegraf UltraLight - what Hall of Femme sets the same
caption in - gives 20.0px, so the same sentence at the same stated
size reads smaller here than it does there.
The capitals do not lose nearly as much: 25.0px against Telegraf's
26.6px, near enough the same. Which of the two numbers a channel
lands on is decided by `uppercase`, and crowned-ladies-nw is where
that decision and its reasons are written out.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file,
and also the name the installer registers the file under when it puts
a copy into Windows (engine.install_fonts takes the first entry).
The full name first and the PostScript name behind it, in that order,
because Windows keys installed fonts by name ID 4 - so the entry the
installer writes and the name a local() can resolve are the same
string. Both name this one cut rather than the family, which is the
whole point of the note above: 'Cormorant Garamond' on its own is
deliberately absent, because it is the name all ten cuts answer to.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice - a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before anything is
drawn. They are still chosen rather than copied, and the choice here
is texturina-18pt-regular's exactly, because the position is: a
literary serif that has to keep being a serif if its file goes
Georgia first - the one serif on every Windows this app runs on that
was drawn for reading on a screen, with hairlines sturdy enough to
survive it. Times New Roman behind it as the floor: a poorer stand-in
for a face this light, since it was drawn for print at newspaper
sizes, but present everywhere and at least a serif.
Impact and Arial Black, which most of this folder falls back through,
are absent for the reason they are absent there. They are heavy sans
display grotesques and this is the opposite of one, so falling back
to either would make the single thing that survives a missing file the
stack: 'Cormorant Garamond Regular', Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif
